header.note: The pages of the interaction plane (architecture §5.7): every string a user reads. ICU message format: {client} is the name of the client, {username} the name of the user.

trans-unit.target: Please sign in again to continue.
{client} requires a stronger sign-in than the one you have.
A stronger sign-in than the one you have is required.
Your password followed by the code of your authenticator app would satisfy it.
Sign-in failed. Check your username and your password, then try again.
{client} also asks to be allowed to:
Who you are: your identifier at this provider
Access while you are away, until you revoke it
You are asked to sign out.
You are signed in as {username}. Do you want to sign out?
This provider cannot serve the request. Start again from the application.
No request is waiting for this page. Start again from the application.
The request took too long. Start again from the application.
The request was already answered. Start again from the application.
The form was not submitted from this provider. Start again from the application.
The application sent a request this provider cannot serve. Start again from the application.
This provider has taken too many requests and did not serve this one. Wait a moment and start again from the application.
No application of this provider begins a sign-in from here. Start again from the application.
The passkey could not be used. Try again, or sign in with your password.
This provider signs you in with your passkey.
This address cannot be read. Check it, then try again.
Your organisation signs you in: no password, passkey or authenticator app of this account signs you in, and none is added to it.
Your organisation signs you in: no passkey is added to this account.
Your organisation signs you in: no authenticator app is set up for this account.
Your organisation signs you in: no password is posed for this account.
{count, plural, =0 {Nothing filled in} one {One detail} other {# details}}
{count, plural, =0 {No passkey} one {One passkey} other {# passkeys}}
{count, plural, =0 {No application} one {One application} other {# applications}}

This is everything this provider holds about you. An application obtains what you allow it to and nothing else; your passkeys, your authenticator app and the applications you have allowed are on the pages of their own.
You have told this provider nothing about yourself.
This browser cannot create a passkey.
The passkey could not be created. Try again.
Give the passkey a name of 1 to 255 characters.
No passkey was being created. Try again.
This provider refused the passkey. Try again with another one.
{client} asks you to sign in. Enter the code shown by your authenticator app, or one of your backup codes.
The code was refused. Try again with the code the app shows now.
This backup code is not valid, or it has already been used. Each backup code works only once.
Too many codes have been tried. Wait a moment, then try again.
An application you have allowed is not asked about again. Taking that back also takes back the access it holds: it asks you afresh the next time you use it.
This provider signs you in with your passkey, so your account needs no authenticator app.
Your account has no authenticator app yet. Once one is set up, a code from it is asked after your password.
An authenticator app is set up since {date}.
{count, plural, =0 {No backup code left} one {# backup code left} other {# backup codes left}}
Scan this QR code with your authenticator app.
Or enter this key by hand:
Your authenticator app is set up. From now on, a code from it is asked after your password.
Keep these backup codes somewhere safe. Each one signs you in once, in place of a code of the app, if you lose it. They are shown only now.
The code does not match. Enter the code the app shows now.
No set-up was in progress, or it took too long. Start again.
An authenticator app is already set up. Remove it before setting up another one.
Sign in, then open this page again.
Your browser is sending you back to the application. If nothing happens, use the button below.
Signing you out of your applications

We have asked the applications you signed into with this account to sign you out. Those your browser lets us reach have been told; your browser may block some of them, and those applications sign you out when you next use them.
Please sign in to continue. Enter the code shown by your authenticator app, or one of your backup codes.
Enter the code your device is showing.
That code is not one we are waiting for. Check the code your device is showing, and enter it again.
Too many codes have been entered from here. Wait a minute and try again.
{client} asks to connect to your account with the code {code}.
an address we could not read
a device that named itself to us
If you did not start this on a device of yours, refuse it. Nobody ever needs a code from you.
{client} may now use your account. Go back to your device; it will continue on its own.
{client} has been refused. Nothing was given to it, and you can close this page.
Nothing is waiting for you. If an application told you otherwise, it was not us.
an address we could not read
a client that named itself to us
If you did not start this yourself, refuse it. Nobody ever needs your approval on their behalf.
That request is no longer waiting for an answer. Here is what is left.
{client} may now use your account. Go back to where you started; it will continue on its own.
{client} has been refused. Nothing was given to it, and you can close this page.

A browser you add here is told when something is waiting for you to answer. What it is told is who is asking and what they wrote; it never carries a request and never answers one, so you always come here to look.
No browser of yours is told.
This browser cannot be told; use one that can show notifications.
This provider does not tell browsers.
This browser was not added. It may have refused notifications.
What this browser sent is not something a push service could be asked to deliver to.
This provider does not tell browsers.
{count, plural, =0 {Nothing waiting for you} one {One request waiting for you} other {# requests waiting for you}}
{count, plural, =0 {No browser told} one {One browser told} other {# browsers told}}
{client} is asking you to approve a sign-in. Open your account to answer.
{client} is asking you to approve: {message}. Open your account to answer.
Each line is a browser or an application holding a session opened in your name. Ending one signs it out everywhere that session reached.
{count, plural, =0 {no session open} one {one session open} other {# sessions open}}
{count, plural, =0 {Nothing it holds can be renewed.} one {One token it holds can still be renewed.} other {# tokens it holds can still be renewed.}}
An access token it was already issued stays usable until it expires, whatever is taken back here; what this provider is asked about it says the truth from that instant.
It is waiting for nothing from you.
It will ask you afresh the next time it needs something, and what it holds stops renewing.

Every act this provider wrote down in your name: the times somebody signed in as you and with what they proved it, the times somebody tried and did not, and what changed of your account. A line you do not recognise is worth a new password.
{count, plural, =0 {no refused attempt} one {# refused attempt} other {# refused attempts}}
A way of signing in was added
A way of signing in was removed
A way of signing in was deleted, this provider no longer allowing it
A way of signing in was renamed
Account created at your first sign-in through your organisation
File of your data asked for
What this provider lets you say of yourself here. An empty field takes back what you had said.
This provider does not let you change here what it holds of you. What is above is what it holds.
This provider does not let you change that here.
That is not a value this provider can hold for that.
Everything this provider holds about you, in one file. Ask for it here; it is built in the background, and you download it once it is ready.
Your account and everything you have said about yourself
How you prove who you are, without the secrets themselves
The accounts you sign in with elsewhere, and what they told us
The groups you belong to, and where each membership comes from
The applications you agreed to, and what each may obtain
Where you are signed in right now
Everything recorded about what you did here
What you have changed of your record, and what it said before
What each application was given of you, and when
You have not asked for your data yet.
Your file is being built. Come back to this page in a few minutes.
Your file was not built. Nothing is working on it any more: ask for a new one, or delete the request.
Your file was kept for a while and is gone. Ask for a new one.

You can also download the same file inside a container only your passphrase opens. Choose a passphrase of at least {minimum} characters, several words rather than a password: nothing here keeps it, so nobody can give it back to you, and it is the only thing standing between that file and whoever ends up holding it. Opening a .{container} encrypted this way needs an archive tool such as 7-Zip or Keka; the file managers built into Windows and macOS do not read it.
That is not a passphrase this file can leave under. Several words, at least {minimum, number} characters.
A file is kept for {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}, then deleted.
the last request was not built
You have not changed anything of your record yet.
Every change you have made to your own record, the most recent first. What a client of this provider reads is the record as it is now.
You changed nothing over those days.
The days this table is read over
That is not a name a browser can hold. Type between 1 and 255 characters.
Once you have the file, this provider has no reason to keep it. Deleting it here takes it away now rather than on the date above.
There was nothing to delete. It may have gone away already.
No session is open in your name.
No session of yours was opened over those days.
You allowed no application over those days.
Nothing was recorded over those days.
No browser of yours was added over those days.
You enrolled no passkey over those days.
You hold no password: you sign in by another means. Nothing to replace here.
Type the password you use now, then the one you want instead. Every other browser signed in as you is signed out; this one stays.
That is not the password you use now.
That is the password you already have. Pose another one.
You hold no password: there is nothing to replace.
This password has been found in a list of compromised passwords ({date}): somebody else holds it. Replace it now.
You are here instead of the page you were going to. Replace your password and you will carry on there; leave this page and you will be asked again at your next sign-in.
A password is at least {minimum} characters long.
That is longer than a password can be.
That password is too easy to guess. Make it longer, or use several words; nothing has to be a capital, a digit or a symbol.
That password has been found in a list of compromised passwords: somebody else already holds it. Pose another one.
The list of compromised passwords could not be reached, so nothing was written. Try again.
The two passwords you typed are not the same.
{days, plural, =0 {written today} one {written yesterday} other {written # days ago}}
